newsitem.title: USA: Traders say USDA data bullish for CME live cattle.
newsitem.headline: Traders say USDA data bullish for CME live cattle.

text.p: Livestock analysts and traders called the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Cattle-On-Feed Report bullish for Chicago Mercantile Exchange live cattle futures.

They said USDA's December placements figure of 98 percent of a year ago for feedlots in the seven key states was surprising low and should have April and June live cattle contracts opening 0.50 to 1.00 cent per lb higher at Monday's opening.
The February live cattle contract may open 0.25 to 0.50 cent higher, they said.
"This placement number is very bullish to futures," said independent livestock analyst, Phil Stanley.
February live cattle futures were expected 0.25 to 0.50 cent per lb higher and April and June 0.50 to 1.00 cent higher.
Feeder cattle futures were expected to open 0.25 to 0.50 cent a lb higher, especially after Friday's sell-off, traders said.
